cohort: 30 singleton pregnancies with short femur and humerus, compared to 60 pregnancies with normal fetal bone lengths
finding: Euploid and nonanomalous pregnancies with isolated short long bones have a significantly higher risk of adverse pregnancy outcomes, including preterm delivery, preeclampsia, pathologic umbilical Doppler flow, lower birth weight, stillbirth, early neonatal death, and emergency cesarean delivery.
mod_finding: The risk of emergency cesarean delivery was significantly higher in the group with short long bones.
birth_weight: Significantly lower in the group with short fetal femur and humerus
